en: Although many celebrate July 4, Philippine Independence Day is officially on June 12, marking Emilio Aguinaldo's 1898 declaration.
While Jose Rizal is the national hero, Emilio Aguinaldo actually served as the first President of the Philippines.
Contrary to popular belief, Andres Bonifacio founded the Katipunan secret society, not the exiled Jose Rizal.
The Philippine Congress is not just the Senate; it is a bicameral body comprising both the Senate and House of Representatives.
The Barong Tagalog is not made of thick fabric, but rather delicate, translucent piña cloth to prove the wearer is unarmed.
The Tinikling dance did not originate from Spanish royalty, but from Visayan farmers mimicking tikling birds dodging bamboo traps.
Filipino is the national language, but the Philippines does not have just one language, as it recognizes over 130 regional languages.
The Philippine President cannot serve multiple terms, as the Constitution strictly limits them to a single six-year term without re-election.
Emilio Aguinaldo designed the flag, but Marcela Agoncillo and her daughter Lorenza actually sewed the first official Philippine flag.
Many think Fe del Mundo only practiced locally, but she was actually the first woman admitted to Harvard Medical School in 1936.
The Department of Education does not manage universities; it handles basic education, while the Commission on Higher Education oversees colleges.
Filipino citizens do not need to wait until age 21 to vote, as the legal voting age is actually 18.
